subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 71-year-old man with myelodysplastic syndrome has worsening anemia and neutropenia with 8% blasts in the bone marrow. He is treated with azacitidine. Follow-up marrow shows increased expression of genes that were previously hypermethylated at their promoter CpG islands.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

options.text: It acetylates histone tails, relaxing chromatin and increasing transcription
It methylates promoter CpG islands, silencing the affected genes
It intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II
It inhibits DNA methyltransferase, reversing promoter hypermethylation and gene silencing
It inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase, depleting guanine nucleotides

explanation_correct: Azacitidine is a cytidine analog that inhibits DNA methyltransferase, causing hypomethylation of promoter CpG islands and re-expression of silenced genes. Methylation within gene promoters (CpG islands) normally represses transcription.

explanation_incorrect.A: Histone acetylation is produced by histone acetyltransferases; azacitidine does not acetylate histones.
explanation_incorrect.B: CpG methylation silences genes; the drug removes methylation rather than adding it.
explanation_incorrect.C: Topoisomerase II inhibitors such as etoposide and teniposide cause double-stranded DNA breaks; that is not the mechanism here.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mycophenolate mofetil inhibits inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase; it is an immunosuppressant and not the drug described.

educationalObjective: DNA methylation of promoter CpG islands represses transcription, and DNA methyltransferase inhibitors reverse this silencing.
